name: Eliasaph
overview: Eliasaph was a male leader from the tribe of Gad during the time of the Exodus. He served as the head of the tribe of Gad at the time of the census, playing a significant role in the organization of Israel's camp. His leadership is specifically noted in the book of Numbers during the wilderness period.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliasaph means 'G-d has added,' reflecting a recognition of God's provision or blessing. This proper name is recorded in Numbers 1:14, highlighting his identity as a divinely acknowledged leader within Israel.
familyAndRelationships: Eliasaph is identified as the son of Deuel, establishing a direct familial connection that situates him within the lineage of the tribe of Gad. Beyond this relationship, Scripture does not record additional family details about him.
scriptureSignificance: Eliasaph's role as the head of the tribe of Gad during the census underscores his importance in the orderly arrangement and leadership of Israel during the Exodus. His mention affirms God's providential governance through appointed leaders, ensuring the tribe's readiness and participation in the journey to the Promised Land. This leadership position reflects God's ongoing work in organizing His people for His purposes.
